chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban, from Dharih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever five years pass for him and he does not perform Hajj to his Lord, while he is affluent, indeed he is deprived.

key_terms.مُوسِرٌ: Affluent or wealthy person with means to perform Hajj
key_terms.يَفِدْ: To travel or go for pilgrimage (specifically Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a wealthy person who delays performing Hajj for five years?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the timeframe for the obligation of Hajj, specifying that a five-year period is the standard window for an affluent person to fulfill this duty. The term 'mahroom' (deprived) signifies spiritual loss and exclusion from divine mercy, emphasizing that financial capacity alone does not exempt one from the urgency of performing Hajj. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that delaying Hajj beyond this period without valid excuse constitutes a neglect of a fundamental pillar of Islam.
